steps.description: Parse input data and build data structures for jobs, operations, machines, downtimes and policy
Determine precedence-aware repair order: sort operations by (index, baseline start, base index)
Implement overlap detection function using half-open intervals [s,e)

failure_patterns.reason: ⚠️ Use half-open intervals [s,e). Correct formula: 's < b and a < e'. Using <= causes false positives when intervals touch at boundaries (e.g., [a,b) and [b,c) don't overlap)

suggestions: Overlap is defined as half-open interval collision: return s < b and a < e (where [a,b) and [s,e) are the two intervals).
warnings: Never use <= in the overlap check — adjacent intervals [a,b) and [b,c) must NOT be considered overlapping.

steps.description: Implement has_conflict to check both machine timeline conflicts and scheduled downtime conflicts
Implement earliest_feasible_time with incremental forward scan (t += 1) from anchor

failure_patterns.reason: ⚠️ Must scan forward incrementally (t += 1) from anchor. Jumping to 'next gap' or using binary search breaks the minimality requirement — you must find the EARLIEST feasible time, not just any feasible time.

suggestions: Scan forward from anchor one unit at a time: while has_conflict(m, t, t+dur): t += 1.

steps.description: Repair operations in precedence-aware order and track ALL operations (including frozen) in machine_intervals

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ CRITICAL: Even frozen operations MUST be added to machine_intervals! If you skip adding them with 'if frozen: continue', later operations will overlap with frozen ones, causing machine conflicts. Always call machine_intervals[m].append((start, end)) for ALL operations, including frozen ones.

warnings: Frozen operations still occupy machine time — always record them in machine_intervals even if you cannot change their schedule.

steps.description: Output the fully repaired schedule respecting all precedence, machine, and policy constraints
